title: The Art of War
published_date: c. 5th century BCE (compiled over the Warring States period)

access.edition_or_version: Classical text; consulted via reference-level description of the text and its attributed authorship

mechanics.premise: A classical Chinese treatise on strategy that repeatedly treats time, speed and momentum as decisive resources.
mechanics.tone_function: Cross-cultural anchor for the idea that urgency is a property of the situation (the moment of advantage) rather than of emotional volume.
mechanics.time_handling: Speed and timely action are framed as strategic goods; delay is a lost position, not merely an emotional failure.
mechanics.conceptual_vocabulary: The classical notion of strategic configuration / momentum (shi) and the value of the opportune moment overlap functionally with kairos, though the traditions are not equivalent.
mechanics.cultural_scope: Warring States Chinese strategy; engagement is analogical and explicitly bounded, not an assertion of translatability.
mechanics.translation_limits: The text is compiled and its authorship attributed; key terms such as shi resist one-word English rendering.
mechanics.verification_note: Sun Tzu and the text's traditional attribution described via reference summary; marked partial because no single translation was page-inspected and key-term analysis would need specialist verification.
